lessons.title: Logic & Proof
lessons.content:
KEY CONCEPTS: Discrete math studies distinct, separate values — the mathematics of computation. Propositional logic: statements that are true or false, combined with AND (∧), OR (∨), NOT (¬), IMPLIES (→). Truth tables evaluate compound statements. Logical equivalences (De Morgan's laws: ¬(A∧B) = ¬A∨¬B). Predicate logic adds quantifiers: ∀ (for all), ∃ (there exists). Proof techniques: direct proof, proof by contradiction, proof by contrapositive, and mathematical induction (prove base case, then that each case implies the next — like dominoes).

WORKED EXAMPLE: Prove that if n² is even, then n is even, by contrapositive: assume n is odd (n=2k+1), then n² = 4k²+4k+1 = 2(2k²+2k)+1, which is odd. Since 'n odd → n² odd' is proven, its contrapositive 'n² even → n even' holds. Contrapositive proof turns a hard direct proof into an easy one — a core technique of rigorous reasoning.

PRACTICE: 1) Build a truth table for A → B. 2) State De Morgan's laws. 3) Explain how mathematical induction works.
